attributes.other_names: Banso, Bansaw, Bansso, Banzo, Nsaw, Lamnso (also used for the language). The Nso' take their name from their founder Ngonnso'.
attributes.home: The Bamenda Grassfields in the Northwest Region, mainly Bui Division.
attributes.capital: Kumbo (also called Kimbo), where the Fon's palace stands.
attributes.size: Estimates differ. About 240,000 speakers of Lamnso' (2005 estimate), about 217,000 people on 2,300 square kilometres in one source, and 401,000 Nso in Cameroon in a Joshua Project profile.
attributes.standing: Described as the largest ethnic group of the Northwest Region.
attributes.classification: Considered a subgroup of the Tikar by one reference.
attributes.ba_prefix: Banso means people of Nso. Sources disagree on the Ba- prefix: one attributes it to Fulani conquerors in the 17th century, another says such forms came from foreign influence.
attributes.economy: An agricultural society. Women are the farmers and are called the backbone of the country. Men owned the fields while women owned the crops.
attributes.languages_in_use: Lamnso', Cameroon Pidgin English, English, Limbum and Oku.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus Nso and Its Neighbours (2011) and 101 Last Tribes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.area: Nso', Oku and Mbiame together form Bui Division.
attributes.bui_division_1976: About 142,000 people, in an area roughly like that of Luxembourg.
attributes.other_fons: Other Fons act as advisers to the Fon of Nso. Most were once leaders of independent groups that came under the Fon of Nso through war, peaceful agreement or events of history. The Fons of Oku and Mbiame were once princes of Nso.
attributes.tikar_dynasties: Nso, Kom, Bafut, Bum and Ndu were five kingdoms with Tikar or Ndobo-derived dynasties that grew in the nineteenth century.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus 101 Last Tribes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

content.name: Origin and migration of the Nso

attributes.origin: The Nso' came from Tikari, in the Adamawa area, after a bloody succession dispute following the death of Chief Tinki in 1387, according to one source.
attributes.leader: Ngonnso', founder of the Nso' dynasty, left Kimi with a few followers and her brothers Nchare Yen and Mbombam with their followers.
attributes.bamum_link: Her brother Nchare Yen is named as the eventual founder of the Bamum kingdom.
attributes.route: After parting from her brothers, Ngonnso' and her followers settled successively at Mbo'nso', Ndzennso' and Kovifem, withdrew to Taavisa for security, returned to Kovifem and finally moved to Kimbo (Kumbo).
attributes.first_german_contact: Lieutenant Kurt von Pavel's first contact with the Nso' was friendly, and he received a ram from the Fon.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Ngonnso (CC BY-SA 4.0), the Prussian Cultural Heritage Foundation, and Quartz. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.role: Founder of the Nso' dynasty and first queen mother of the Nso kingdom, revered as a mother deity.
attributes.name_meaning: Means young lady of Nso, according to Quartz.
attributes.legend: She left a succession conflict with her brothers Nchare Yen and Mbombam and led her followers to Kumbo.
attributes.statue: The statue that represents her was taken in colonial times and is now in Berlin.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus the Vestiges journal and the Wikipedia Fon (title) page. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.role: Head of the traditional government and the chief religious authority, in charge of keeping the ancestors happy.
attributes.name: Sehm Mbinglo I is named as the Fon in several Wikipedia articles and photo captions, while one passage says Sehm Mbinglo II as of 2013.
attributes.earlier_fon: Fon Ngah Bifon I reigned from 1910 to 1947.
attributes.limits: His power is checked by regulatory societies such as the Ngwerong.
attributes.caution: Check who holds the office now, because the sources date from 2013 or earlier.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus 101 Last Tribes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.role: A regulatory society that is in effect the security arm of the government and enforces the decisions of the Fon.
attributes.enthronement: It alone is responsible for the enthronement of a new Fon.
attributes.members: All the Fons of Nso and Shufai Ndzendzev belong to both the Ngwerong and the Ngiri.
attributes.masked_spirits: Ngwerong and Ngiri each have seven jujus, often seen on the way to a member's death celebration.

source.citation: 101 Last Tribes, Nso people, and Wikipedia, Nso people. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: The princes' society of the Nso.
attributes.members: The Fons of Nso and Shufai Ndzendzev belong to it and to the Ngwerong.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus 101 Last Tribes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: A traditional warrior society of the Nso.
attributes.note: When a member has celebrated Mfu well, the drums come out for dancing.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.fai: A leader of a lineage group. Nso society is divided into groups by lineage, each led by a Fai who is instituted by the Fon.
attributes.etiquette: Tradition says a Fai's hand is not shaken.
attributes.appearance: Fais are recognised by glass bead necklaces and fancy walking sticks.
attributes.shey: Other leaders called Sheys are a level below the Fais.
attributes.princes: Princes are called Wontho and meet in the presence of the Fon to discuss family matters.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Nso people (CC BY-SA 4.0). Plus 101 Last Tribes. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: Jujus are masked spirits and an important part of Nso culture.
attributes.occasions: They come out on important occasions, and the passing of a juju led by its handlers and followed by children is a street performance.
attributes.music: Other jujus are groups that dance to drums and xylophones. Music and the skilful use of traditional melodies are central to Nso culture.

source.citation: 101 Last Tribes, Nso people, and a news feature on Ngonnso'. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.description: A cultural week that brings together the traditions of the Nso and neighbouring peoples, with jujus on display from the palace to the other quarters of Kumbo.
attributes.attendance: Tens of thousands of people attend the multi-day festival every year, according to a news feature on Ngonnso'.
attributes.date_note: The date is not recorded here.

source.citation: Open Mythology Collection (University of Warsaw), item 603, a Nso myth. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.meaning: In Lamnso' it means the stone of God.
attributes.role: The name the Nso give to the God who gives children.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Kumbo (CC BY-SA 4.0), and Atlas Obscura on the Ngonnso statue. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.role: Capital of the Nso kingdom and the seat of the Fon.
attributes.palace: The Nso Palace is the heart of the town's social and cultural life.
attributes.market: The Mbve market is the main market, selling products from the region, Cameroon, Nigeria and elsewhere.
attributes.known_for: Horse racing (Tobin Stadium), traditional medicine, the palace and two hospitals, Shisong Hospital and Banso Baptist Hospital.
attributes.statue: A statue of Ngonnso', the legendary first queen of the Nso, stands in the palace compound. It is a replica made in 2008, since the original is in Berlin.

source.citation: Wikipedia, Kumbo (CC BY-SA 4.0), and a Banso culture page. Compiled for this collection and not yet reviewed by a second person.

attributes.location: The Kumbo area, in Nso country.
attributes.services: Hosts a nursing school, a network of clinics, an HIV management programme and a surgical residency.

attributes.mission: To propagate Nso' cultural heritage, support the arts and crafts of the Western Grassfields, and make them known in Cameroon and internationally.
attributes.collection: Includes utensils made by the Grassfields peoples of the Northwest and West.
attributes.note: Describes masterpieces of Grassfields art held in foreign museums.

attributes.arrival: Islam became prominent in Nso and in Bui Division during German rule.
attributes.traders: Hausa traders were linked with its spread.
